biography: Born in the shadow of Silverstone, Ron Linn practically inhaled the scent of high-octane fuel from infancy. His father, a former club racer, gifted him a kart at age seven, sparking an obsession that consumed his adolescence. Early promise was evident, but a tendency for impulsive decisions plagued his progress. A defining moment came at the Ginetta Junior Championship, where, leading comfortably, he tangled with a lapped car on the final corner, gifting the win to his rival. This costly mistake fueled a relentless focus on consistency, though the old demons occasionally resurface. Now, at 28, and considered to be at his peak, Linn aims to use his experience to make him a consistent race winner.
drivingStyle: Linn possesses a raw speed that's undeniable, often extracting more from the Ginetta than it seems capable of. His corner entry is aggressive, bordering on reckless, but his car control is exceptional, allowing him to dance on the edge of adhesion. Tire management is a work in progress; he tends to push too hard early in stints, leaving him vulnerable in the closing laps. Under pressure, Linn can either rise to the occasion with a moment of brilliance or succumb to the mistakes of his past.

rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track battle at Brands Hatch in 2021 resulted in a controversial collision, sparking a bitter feud that continues to this day.
Thorne, a meticulous and calculating driver, is the antithesis of Linn, creating a clash of styles and personalities that often boils over on the track.
Carter and Linn came through the karting ranks together and a series of intense battles left a mark, fuelling a competitive edge every time they share the track.

quirks: Always wears a specific pair of lucky racing socks passed down from his father.
Insists on having a pre-race cup of Earl Grey tea, regardless of the weather or location.
Repeats a silent mantra - "Smooth is fast" - three times before every qualifying session.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about taming the beast within."
careerHighlight: Winning the Ginetta GT4 Supercup Championship in 2020 with a dominant display at Donington Park, securing the title with a race to spare.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Silverstone 24 Hours in 2022 due to a momentary lapse in concentration, costing his team a shot at victory.
